verdict.rationale: Anrok documents that each product gets a product tax category that determines its taxability in each jurisdiction, which directly addresses state-by-state SaaS taxability. Its AI Atlas claims answers with the reasoning shown, though that is a Q&A feature rather than research attached to each determination. Missing for 10: explicit digital-goods rule handling, bundled-offering taxability, per-determination research or citations visible in the product, and independent or hands-on corroboration of accuracy on hard cases.

support.subject: As a founder selling software, the product gets the hard cases right — SaaS taxability that differs by state, digital-goods rules, and bundled offerings — with the research behind each determination visible

citations.quote: Each product is identified by an external ID and is assigned a product tax category (PTC) which determines the product's taxability in each jurisdiction.
Anrok sellers only need to create product IDs for each unique tax category, not every single product in the catalog.
Ask it anything about your sales tax and get an answer with the reasoning shown, grounded in your own transactions, registrations, filings, and certificates.
